en.title: Comparatives
en.goal: Compare people and things using plus, moins and aussi... que.

blocks.title: Plus... que (more... than)
blocks.body: To say that something has "more" of a quality than something else, you use plus + adjective + que. It's the most common comparison structure in French.
examples: My brother is taller than me.
This dress is prettier than the other one.

blocks.title: Moins... que / aussi... que
blocks.body: On the other side, moins... que expresses inferiority ("less... than") and aussi... que expresses equality ("as... as"). The structure is always the same; only the little word in the middle changes.
examples: She is less tall than him.
He is as kind as his brother.

blocks.title: An irregularity: bon → meilleur
blocks.body: Just like in English "good" doesn't become "more good" but "better", in French bon also breaks the pattern: there is no "plus bon" — the correct form is meilleur. The same happens with the adverb bien (well), which becomes mieux (better) in the comparative.
examples: This cake is better than the other one.

blocks.title: Très bien! 🎉
blocks.body: Recapping the three comparison structures and the bon/bien exception — it's worth memorizing this table, because bon → meilleur is a very common mistake among beginners:

review.pt: Ela é menos alta que ele.
review.en: She is less tall than him.
review.why: kept literal to mirror 'moins grande'; natural English would be 'shorter than him'

review.pt: Ele é tão gentil quanto o irmão.
review.en: He is as kind as his brother.

review.pt: Assim como em português "bom" não vira "mais bom"...
review.en: Just like in English "good" doesn't become "more good"...
review.why: comparison with Portuguese adapted to English (same irregularity good → better); content adapted
